selection: Three questions selected before this full-text screen; these are not a representative estimate of the entire 1,006-paper frame.

label_rubric.ineligible_at_cutoff: The original cutoff-version paper itself directly tests the broad proposed question; retain only a scientifically distinct, narrower unresolved extension.
label_rubric.eligible_unresolved_at_cutoff: The original cutoff-version source describes a question for which it does not itself report the specified direct outcome measure.
label_rubric.followup_direct_resolution: A dated later primary source within the frozen three-year window evaluates the same intervention/control, outcome, and target population sufficiently to test the stated question.
label_rubric.no_direct_followup_adjudicated: The inspected follow-ups do not meet the direct-resolution criterion; this does not prove that no such study exists elsewhere. Do not code as a negative scientific result.

cutoff_evidence.finding: Authors directly compare HsuanFuzz with and without TCL feedback, plus RESTler; on RealWorld after 200 wall-clock seconds their table reports 610 versus 576 covered lines for the two HsuanFuzz arms.

Authors run 24-hour Spree/Magento comparisons and state the two HsuanFuzz arms yield similar eventual error sets on Magento; the reported benefit is largely earlier discovery in their time curve, not a shown long-run unique-bug advantage.

The abstract calls 351 remote findings bugs, but IV-3 defines them as HTTP 500 responses in 47 remote services, with 465 greater-than-500 responses in 64; independent defect confirmation is not shown there.
The paper reports 14 Spree plus 75 Magento errors confirmed as bugs in linked project issues. These are authors' grouped claims, not 89 independently re-executed distinct defects in this audit.

rows.research_decision: Down-rank the broad novelty claim; a balanced, equal-CPU/requests, verified distinct-bug replication is a narrower experiment, subject to feasibility and further prior-art review.

cutoff_evidence.finding: The paper measures NVD field inconsistencies and compares retrospective analyses with a rectified NVD. It proposes practical applications, but does not evaluate whether deploying the corrections prospectively improves vulnerability triage against later independently verified outcomes.

rows.research_decision: Retain as a Level-1 candidate requiring versioned NVD snapshots, fixed alert budget, and verified later security outcomes; do not infer benefit from retrospective analysis changes or user reports.

cutoff_evidence.finding: The authors already evaluate resampling, random seeds and alternative ML-library implementations using 26 SE datasets and eight classifiers; they report variable performance. A general claim that these factors had not yet been tested was therefore invalid at the 2020 cutoff.

rows.research_decision: Down-rank the original broad lead as already studied; a new framework-version or distribution-shift claim needs a distinct preregistered test.

limitations: This is a purposive three-paper screen, not a prevalence estimate across CS.
Original full texts were read through arXiv HTML/PDF views; no local PDF checksum was recorded for these three in this checkpoint.
Follow-up review was targeted, not exhaustive; no absence-of-evidence label is an unresolved-science outcome.
Project issues corroborate grouped confirmation labels for some original claims but were not independently replayed or de-duplicated here.
